title: ee.mesh.surrogate.v1
description: Compatibility, privacy, and rebuild metadata for a single search surrogate (embedding, summary, minhash, lexical metadata, or query fingerprint) attached to a memory that may cross a mesh peer boundary. The surrogate metadata is the contract that lets a peer decide whether the surrogate can be locally indexed, whether it must be recomputed against the local model, or whether the local node must fall back to lexical-only search. Default-deny applies: a surrogate is unavailable for export unless the peer policy explicitly allows the matching `surrogateType` lane.

memoryId.description: Optional reference to the memory whose body or query produced this surrogate. Required for memory-attached surrogates; omitted for ephemeral query fingerprints.

contentHash.description: Hash of the source content that produced this surrogate. Used by `surrogate_recomputed` decisions to detect that the local content already matches and a remote surrogate is safe to attach without recomputation.

validUntil.description: Optional staleness boundary. When absent the surrogate is treated as fresh until the model fingerprint or content hash changes.

degradedCode.description: When the surrogate is rendered into a structured-log or status surface as a degradation, the emitted code must be one of these documented values. See `repair_present` fixtures under `tests/fixtures/failure_modes/` once the matching Rust constants land.

surrogateType.description: The shape of the surrogate. Each type is treated as an independent lane by mesh peer policy: a peer may allow `lexical_metadata` while denying `embedding`, for example.

modelFingerprint.description: Identifies the producer of the surrogate so the receiver can run a compatibility check. Two surrogates are compatible iff `modelId` and `modelVersion` match exactly; `featureFlags` capture optional model-side configuration (quantization mode, normalization, tokenizer revision) that callers must also match before reusing a remote surrogate without recomputation.

policy.description: Surrogate-level privacy and rebuild rules. `exportAllowed=false` is the project-wide default; the field must be present explicitly so that an absent value cannot accidentally widen the export surface. `requiresLocalRecompute=true` instructs the receiver to drop the surrogate payload, fetch the source content (subject to mesh body-fetch policy), and recompute under the local model — emitting `surrogate_recomputed`. `requiresCompatibilityCheck=true` instructs the receiver to compare `modelFingerprint` against its local model; if they differ the receiver must emit `surrogate_incompatible` and fall back to `lexical_fallback_used`. When the policy itself denies the lane, the receiver emits `surrogate_denied`.

lexicalFallback.description: When the surrogate cannot be served (denied, incompatible, or stale), should the receiver fall back to lexical metadata? Default true; set false to fail closed instead.
